title: Sections at an algebraically closed point commute with finite coefficient reduction
statement:
Let $\kappa$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $t=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with its small pro-etale site $t_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $\Gamma(t,-)$ be the sections over the final object $\operatorname{id}_t$, on derived categories [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $\kappa$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_i=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^i$ for $i\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $(A_i)_t$ for the constant sheaf of rings on $t_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], so that $\Gamma(t,(A_i)_t)=A_i$, and $D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},A_i)$, $D(A_i)$ for the derived categories of $(A_i)_t$-modules and of $A_i$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $n\geq j\geq1$ and let $N\in D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ have cohomology sheaves vanishing in all sufficiently large degrees (in particular, $N$ may be cohomologically bounded). This bounded-above domain is preserved by the reductions below. Let $N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\in D(t_{\mathrm{proet}},A_j)$ be the derived change of rings along $(A_n)_t\to(A_j)_t$, and $\Gamma(t,N)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\in D(A_j)$ the derived change of rings along $A_n\to A_j$, both as in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then there is an isomorphism
$$
\Gamma(t,N)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Gamma\bigl(t,N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j\bigr)
$$
in $D(A_j)$, natural in $N$, equal to the identity for $j=n$, and compatible with successive reductions: for $n\geq j\geq i\geq1$ the isomorphism for $(n,i)$ is the composite of the isomorphism for $(n,j)$ reduced to $A_i$ and the isomorphism for $(j,i)$ applied to $N\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j$, under the associativity identifications $(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_j)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_j}A_i\cong-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_n}A_i$.

I compared it with the blueprint main-20261015 prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems.proof.md, Proof (1), lines 1-13. That proof moves the finite reduction through Gamma(s,-) and the stalk without stating why; the item supplies exactly this. I also checked Stacks sites-modules lemma-constant-exact (093J) and the next lemma on sections of constant sheaves tensored with a finitely presented module. Statement: the original text was created by Q78 for bounded objects. The change to bounded-above objects is correct and makes the statement stronger, not weaker. Over A_2, Tor_r(A_1,A_1)=A_1 for every r, so the old successive-reduction clause applied its own comparison to an unbounded object. The only citer uses the item in its steps 1 and 7 on bounded Ra_{X!}K_{n+1} and L ybar^*K_{n+1}, so nothing breaks. The coefficient category is right: constant (A_i)_t on the small pro-etale site of any algebraically closed point. The base change is lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings and the isomorphism lands in D(A_j), not D(A_n). Not a duplicate of lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction (integral O_E->A_n case, s=Spec Fpbar only) or lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor (needs Fpbar and ctf inputs). Steps: (1) the ideals of V/pi^n are the (pi^r), and multiplication by pi^r gives R/pi^{n-r} isomorphic to (pi^r). (2) A discrete constant sheaf is sheafified as continuous functions, using the fpqc-sheaf leaf, open fibres as a Zariski cover and the universal property, so Gamma(t,T_t)=T; then F tensor (R/pi^r)_t = F/pi^rF, and exact sections give eta. (3) Sections of a flat sheaf are flat, by injectivity of I tensor Gamma(F)->Gamma(F) for I=(pi^r) and the finitely-generated-ideal criterion; holds for I=0 and I=R. (4) Good truncation and the bounded-above flat replacement make P and C=Gamma(P) K-flat. (5) The chain isomorphism C/pi^jC -> Gamma(P/pi^jP) is B-linear. (6) Naturality comes from the bounded-below localization node applied in the opposite category, then the localization universal property (2); resolution independence via P(S). (7) P_j stays termwise flat over B_t and bounded above. (8) Both routes send [[x]] to the class of x; j=n gives the identity. Edge cases checked: zero object and shifts, n=j=i=1, j=n, i=j, r=0 and r=n, and empty site objects. The hypothesis 'l invertible in kappa' is unused but harmless. All 14 declared tool uses are generic and accepted. No SGA source, no cycle, no new nodes, no changes.
